name: Doorman
slug: Gerk's Doorman role and doorway ability
description: The Doorman is Gerk’s unique keeper role, tied to his Midgard keystone and distinct from the Gatekeeper roles held by the other party members. The role allows Gerk to open and close an Arch, connect with and protect it, and create seamless doorways through reality by manipulating an invisible handle or concentrating on a destination he can conceptualize. These doorways have no conventional threshold and can connect locations directly, remaining open for Gerk or others to pass through rather than necessarily closing automatically. Their destinations are not yet fully predictable, and using the ability requires a Wisdom saving throw. Doorways can produce powerful and unpredictable spatial effects, including stretching or distorting surrounding matter and exerting strong pulling forces, particularly when opened from a moving vessel.

log.summary: The Doorman role was established as distinct from the other party members’ Gatekeeper roles, granting Gerk the ability to open, close, connect with, and protect an Arch. Gerk demonstrated the power by manipulating an invisible handle to create a seamless doorway through reality, without a conventional threshold; his first demonstrated doorway led to an unknown beach on Midgard.

log.summary: Gerk’s Doorman role allows him to open a doorway from his current location to a place he can conceptualize, including known locations such as his own house or Mahali’s stronghold. Using the ability requires a Wisdom saving throw and may also trigger Strength saves when the doorway exerts powerful pulling forces. The doorway can remain open as Gerk or others pass through rather than closing automatically. When opened from a moving boat, the fixed doorway interacts unpredictably with the moving vessel, stretching surrounding space and parts of the boat and producing severe spatial or reality-tear effects. The ability appears to connect locations across space and may involve unusual interactions with time and space. The consequences of closing a doorway under these conditions remain unknown.

log.summary: Dana treats a lingering spectral door as a product of Gerk’s Doorman role and does not expect ordinary Dispel Magic to dismiss keystone-level Doorman magic; that door lasted about a day and ended on its own. Gerk can open a door without choosing a destination. An opening in Carlkin’s lighthouse, from a d100 roll of 68, led to the abyss. Fifth-level Dispel Magic did not close or dismiss it, and Sylan could not end it. Sylan treats these doorways as Gerk’s to close.

log.summary: Carlkin treats doorway practice as rules worth writing down: do not open a doorway on a moving thing or to an unknown place. Opening with no destination opens onto nowhere—the nothing, the astral, or the gap between arches—and correct use is to picture one specific familiar door and open it as if by hand. A portal on a moving ship stays fixed and can tear reality or become a three-way connection. Mastery and wide travel could allow openings nearly anywhere, but a keystone-bound Doorman should expect requests tied to that keystone. Other people besides Gerk can open doors, though Carlkin does not name them; a keystone is generally used by a gatekeeper or a doorman, and long study or a purpose-built gate can work around that. Doorman is the rank above footman: doormen were the more prestigious rank and taught footmen, their apprentices. Carlkin will not grant Gerk the Doorman title yet and calls him a footman until he earns it. As Carlkin tells the legends, the role is Gerk’s own choice; Sylan identified him and brought him the news.
